what.text: Refugees from Myanmar have fled to Bangladesh, where year-end totals rose from 160000 in 1978 to 1178003 in 2025.
While Bangladesh hosts the largest group of refugees from Myanmar, others live in Malaysia, Thailand, India, and Japan.

why.text: Under the 1982 Myanmar citizenship law, the Rohingya were not listed among recognised national groups, leaving most without citizenship.

Displacement occurred alongside the Armed conflict over Arakan territory between the Government of Myanmar and opposition groups including CPA, RPF, and ALP from 1973 to 1978, RSO in 1991 and 1994, ARSA and ULA from 2016 to 2020, and ULA from 2022 to 2025.
In August 2017, mass flight followed attacks by ARSA and military operations in Rakhine State, leading to an investigation by a United Nations fact-finding mission in 2018.
Following a military takeover in 2021, the Armed conflict over the government of Myanmar was active from 2021 to 2025 involving opposition groups NUG, PSLF, CNF, and PNLO.

when.text: An early large exodus occurred in 1978, followed by a second wave from 1991 to 1992 that brought refugee counts in Bangladesh to 244994 by the end of 1992.
Returns to Myanmar followed in subsequent years, but arrivals accelerated after August 2017, bringing the year-end total in Bangladesh to 932204 by the end of 2017.
Joint registration of refugees concluded in 2019, while the main displacement period continued through 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took from Myanmar to Bangladesh.
Reporting notes that refugees reside in camps located in Cox's Bazar and Bhasan Char, which are counted together in the data.
These refugee figures reflect year-end totals of people from Myanmar residing in Bangladesh who are counted under UNHCR's mandate.
